**Repaired finding submitted: deviation (T4C), fallback target.**

Response to the deterministic failure ("Customer convenience termination present"):

- **Diagnosis:** the prior draft left AP with *no* convenience exit during the Initial Term — the lock-in was mutual ("Neither Party may terminate ... during the Initial Term") and the 90-day right operated only "following the Initial Term". So there was no unqualified, presently-available Customer convenience right.
- **Repair (one operation, two surgical touches):**
  - "Neither Party may" → "Kubient may not", so the Initial Term lock-in binds only Kubient;
  - deleted "following the Initial Term", so AP may terminate for any reason at any time on 90 days' written notice;
  - retained proviso, now narrowed to "under this sentence" per the verifier's tightening note, so it cannot be read to reach Kubient's 4(b) breach or insolvency terminations.
- **Coverage:** Customer 90-day right, Vendor's 90-day notice (mutual "notice to the other Party" retained verbatim) and the end-of-term confinement all sit in operation 1; the three-months fee cap remains `already_met` on the untouched fee sentence.
- **Minimality/intent:** gate ok:true; the auto-renewal sentence, fee entitlement, cure period and insolvency rights are untouched, the "paragraph 4(b)" cross-reference still resolves, and no extras (refund mechanics, survival tails, "in whole or in part") were added.
